title: What Happens at a Home Care Assessment Visit? (What to Expect)
short_title: What happens at a home care assessment visit
description: Thinking about home care for Mom or Dad? Here's what happens at a free in-home assessment with Caring Companions, start to finish: the first call, the visit, the care plan, real prices, other ways to pay, matching a caregiver, and meeting their profile before the first visit.

parts.head: What happens at a home care assessment visit?
parts.sub: Start to finish, so there are no surprises
parts.text: You've decided to look into home care. So what actually happens at the assessment visit? I'm Samantha with Caring Companions in Springfield. Here's what to expect, start to finish, so there are no surprises.

parts.head: You reach out
parts.sub: We call within 24 hours to set up the visit
parts.text: It starts when you call us, book online, or fill out our care questionnaire. You don't need to know what kind of care you want yet. Most families don't. A care coordinator reaches out within twenty-four hours to set up the visit.

parts.head: Free, with no obligation
parts.sub: No decision that day. Everything in writing.
parts.text: The assessment is free, and there's no obligation. You don't have to decide anything that day. We listen, answer your questions, and leave everything in writing.

parts.head: We come to the home
parts.sub: The stairs, the bathroom, the lighting
parts.text: We do it in the home, because the home is half the picture: the stairs, the bathroom, the lighting, how far the bedroom is from the kitchen.

parts.head: We get to know your loved one
parts.sub: Routines, what they enjoy, what's getting hard
parts.text: Mostly, we get to know your loved one and your family. Their routines, what they enjoy, what's getting hard, and what matters most to them.

parts.head: A care plan for your situation
parts.sub: What help, when, and what it will cost
parts.text: Then we write a care plan for your situation, not a package off a shelf. What help is needed, when it's really needed, and what it will cost.

parts.head: $30, $32 or $34 an hour
parts.sub: At least 4 hours a visit, 8 a week. No deposit, no contract.
parts.text: We'll recommend the right level together: Wellness Care, Personal Care, or Advanced Care, at thirty, thirty-two, or thirty-four dollars an hour. Visits are at least four hours, and at least eight hours a week. There's no deposit, and no long-term contract.

parts.head: We'll tell you if something fits better
parts.sub: VA, long-term care insurance, or Missouri Medicaid (CDS)
parts.text: If another way of paying fits better, we'll tell you, like VA benefits or long-term care insurance. And if Missouri Medicaid fits, we'll point you to our sister company, Caring Companions CDS.

parts.head: Ask us anything
parts.sub: Rides, sick days, what caregivers can't do
parts.text: Bring your questions. Families often ask about rides to appointments, what happens if a caregiver is sick, and what caregivers can't do. We're non-medical home care, so caregivers remind about medicines, but can't give them.

parts.head: We match and train a caregiver
parts.text: Once you're ready, we match a caregiver by skills, personality, and schedule, and train them on the care plan before they walk through the door.

parts.head: You meet them first
parts.sub: Their profile and photo, before the first visit
parts.text: Before the first visit, we send you the caregiver's profile with a friendly photo. Then we call to confirm the day, the time, and who's coming.

parts.head: We check the fit
parts.sub: Not right? We work it out, or match someone else.
parts.text: A few days after the first visit, we call to see how it's going. And if the fit isn't right, tell us. We'll work it out, or match someone else.
Book your free in-home assessment at mo-care.com, or call us at (417) 234-8494. I'm Samantha with Caring Companions. Thanks for watching.
